name: Sun
tagline: The blazing heart of our solar system
atmosphere: Photosphere → chromosphere → corona, where the plasma reaches 1–3 million °C.
composition: 73% hydrogen, 25% helium, 2% heavier elements — a giant ball of plasma held together by gravity.
facts: The Sun contains 99.86% of ALL mass in the solar system — everything else is a rounding error.
Sunlight takes 8 minutes 20 seconds to reach Earth.
Every second it fuses ~600 million tons of hydrogen into helium.
It is ~4.6 billion years old — roughly halfway through its life.
One million Earths could fit inside it.

name: Mercury
atmosphere: Almost none — just a thin exosphere of oxygen, sodium, hydrogen, helium and potassium blasted off its surface.
composition: A giant iron core (~85% of the radius) wrapped in a thin silicate mantle and cratered crust.
facts: Smallest planet in the solar system — only slightly bigger than our Moon.
A single solar day on Mercury (176 Earth days) is LONGER than its year (88 days).
Temperature swings of ~600 °C between day and night — the most extreme of any planet.
Its surface is covered in craters, just like the Moon.
It is slowly shrinking as its huge iron core cools.

name: Venus
tagline: Earth's evil twin, wrapped in acid clouds
atmosphere: Crushing CO₂ (96.5%) at 92× Earth's pressure, with sulfuric acid clouds. A runaway greenhouse world.
composition: Iron core and silicate mantle; ~90% of the surface is relatively young volcanic rock.
facts: Hottest planet — even hotter than Mercury — because of its runaway greenhouse effect.
It spins BACKWARDS: the Sun rises in the west on Venus.
Its day is longer than its year.
The brightest natural object in our sky after the Sun and Moon.
Surface pressure would crush a submarine at 900 m ocean depth.

name: Earth
tagline: The only known world with life
atmosphere: 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, 1% argon + trace CO₂ — the only known atmosphere that supports life.
composition: Iron-nickel core, silicate mantle and crust; 71% of the surface is covered by liquid water oceans.
facts: The only place in the entire universe where life is confirmed to exist.
71% of the surface is ocean, yet water is only 0.02% of Earth's mass.
Our Moon acts as a stabilizer — without it Earth's axis would wobble chaotically.
Earth's magnetic field deflects the Sun's charged particles and protects our atmosphere.
Auroras near the poles are solar wind particles hitting the atmosphere.

moons.name: Moon
moons.fact: The 5th largest moon in the solar system — likely born from a giant impact ~4.5 billion years ago.

name: Mars
tagline: The rusty red world of robot explorers
atmosphere: Extremely thin CO₂ (95%) — less than 1% of Earth's pressure. Liquid water boils away instantly.
composition: Iron-rich core and basaltic mantle; iron-oxide (rust) dust paints the surface red.
facts: Home to Olympus Mons — at 21.9 km, the tallest volcano in the solar system.
Valles Marineris is a canyon system stretching 4,000 km — it would span the USA.
Mars has seasons, polar ice caps and ancient dried-up riverbeds and lakes.
It hosts the largest fleet of robot explorers: Curiosity, Perseverance and more.
Its two tiny moons may be captured asteroids.

moons.name: Phobos
moons.fact: Orbits faster than Mars rotates — it rises in the WEST and sets in the east.

moons.name: Deimos
moons.fact: A tiny lumpy moon that may be a captured asteroid.

name: Jupiter
tagline: The king of planets, with a storm older than nations
dayLength: 9.93 hours — the fastest spin of any planet
atmosphere: 90% hydrogen, 10% helium with ammonia and water clouds; the Great Red Spot is a storm wider than Earth.
composition: No solid surface — hydrogen gas deepens into liquid metallic hydrogen around a hot, rocky core.
facts: 2.5× the mass of ALL other planets combined.
The Great Red Spot storm has been raging for over 300 years.
Its 9.9-hour day is the shortest of any planet — it spins so fast it visibly bulges.
The strongest planetary magnetic field — 20,000× Earth's.
Its moon Ganymede is bigger than the planet Mercury.

moons.name: Io
moons.fact: The most volcanic body in the solar system — hundreds of active volcanoes.

moons.name: Europa
moons.fact: Ice shell over a global saltwater ocean — a top candidate for finding alien life.

moons.name: Ganymede
moons.fact: The largest moon in the solar system — even bigger than Mercury.

moons.name: Callisto
moons.fact: The most heavily cratered object known — a 4-billion-year-old time capsule.

name: Saturn
tagline: The jewel of the solar system
atmosphere: 96% hydrogen, 3% helium, with hazy ammonia and helium bands. Powerful hexagonal storms.
composition: A gas giant so light it would float in water — density is just 0.69 g/cm³.
facts: Its rings span 280,000 km yet are only ~10 meters thick in places.
A bizarre hexagon-shaped jet stream swirls around its north pole.
The rings are billions of chunks of water ice — from dust grains to house-sized boulders.
Saturn has 146 confirmed moons — more than any other planet.
It is the least dense planet: it would float in a giant bathtub.

moons.name: Titan
moons.fact: The only moon with a thick atmosphere — it has lakes and rain of liquid methane.

moons.name: Rhea
moons.fact: Saturn's second-largest moon — an icy, cratered world.

moons.name: Enceladus
moons.fact: Geysers of water ice erupt from its hidden subsurface ocean into space.

name: Uranus
atmosphere: 83% hydrogen, 15% helium, 2.3% methane — methane absorbs red light, painting the planet cyan.
composition: An ice giant: a dense water-ammonia 'ocean' over a rocky core, beneath a hydrogen-helium atmosphere.
facts: It rolls around the Sun on its side — tilted at 98 degrees, likely from an ancient impact.
Coldest planetary atmosphere ever measured: -224 °C.
Its faint rings were discovered in 1977, before Voyager 2 flew past in 1986.
Each season on Uranus lasts 21 Earth years.
It was the first planet discovered with a telescope (William Herschel, 1781).

moons.name: Titania
moons.fact: The largest Uranian moon, sliced by immense fault canyons.

moons.name: Oberon
moons.fact: The outermost major moon — dark, ancient and heavily cratered.

moons.name: Miranda
moons.fact: A bizarre patchwork world with cliffs 20 km tall — the tallest in the solar system.

name: Neptune
tagline: The windiest world, found by mathematics
atmosphere: 80% hydrogen, 19% helium, 1.5% methane. Supersonic winds rip up to 2,100 km/h — the fastest anywhere.
composition: An ice giant like Uranus: a deep atmosphere over a water-ammonia mantle and rocky core.
facts: Discovered in 1846 by mathematics — predicted on paper before anyone saw it.
Its winds reach 2,100 km/h — the fastest in the solar system, faster than sound on Earth.
It completed its first full orbit since discovery only in 2011.
Its Great Dark Spot storms appear and vanish within years.
Its moon Triton orbits backwards — a captured Kuiper Belt dwarf planet.

moons.name: Triton
moons.fact: Orbits BACKWARDS and erupts nitrogen geysers — a captured dwarf planet from the Kuiper Belt.
